section: Related Work: 2.1 Variant and phenotype extraction from the biomedical literature
focus: large language model extraction of HGVS variants and HPO phenotypes from full-text case reports evaluated against ClinVar
context: Mission: Find how these systems are evaluated (corpus type: case reports vs clinical notes vs abstracts; per-value provenance; negation/absence handling; comparison to curated databases) and what accuracies they report, up to 2026-11. Do not look for new competitors to benchmark; the only model comparison in the log is Claude vs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under an identical scaffold.. Hypothesis: Most systems output entities or variant-paper links without a verbatim quote per value, collapse 'not reported' into absence, work on abstracts or clinical notes rather than full-text case reports, and score against annotations rather than held-out databases; LLM numeric/count fields are error-prone.

section: Related Work: 2.3 Case-level rare-disease resources, imperfect reference databases, and memorization
focus: ClinVar as reference standard limitations for literature-derived variant curation concordance
context: Mission: Find evidence on how far ClinVar/OMIM can serve as ground truth for literature-derived records, how literature-derived phenotype frequencies deviate from genotype-first or natural-history cohorts, and black-box memorization probes usable on closed models, up to 2026-11.. Hypothesis: Curated case-level corpora do not scale to diseases nobody has curated; databases used as ground truth are themselves incomplete or wrong; benchmarks built from published cases risk training-data leakage.

section: 3. Methodology - 3.5 Held-out ground truth, pre-registration and outcomes
focus: Wilson (Probable Inference, the Law of Succession, and Statistical Inference)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Isolation: code under pipeline/extract never reads reference data; an automated test fails on reference paths or the tokens 'clinvar', 'omim', 'harness'; snapshots live outside the repository; list the other leak paths kept out (log §1.8). References with dates: ClinVar release 2026-10-12 read 2026-10-19 (registered six; re-check 2026-10-21), 09 Nov 2026 for extension and Majeed; OMIM = twelve entry pages frozen by the PI on 2026-10-28 (D-42), clinical synopses not frozen; phenotype.hpoa 2026-09-02 on the harness side only (log §1.3). Reference counts per gene go to Appendix A. Pre-registration v1.0 frozen 2026-10-20 (D-36), tags on commit ef3133e (not yet pushed; OSF registration not made; log §1.5). Headline pooled figures use the five diseases other than HA20 (development disease; D-18) (log §1.1). Outcomes O1-O5 as in log §1.9: O1 claim pool, stratified sample of 250, labels, blinding; rule C (<=4 of 250) with operating characteristics P(pass) 0.99/0.89/0.68/0.44/0.13 at true 0.5/1/1.5/2/3%; what 250 claims can certify (0 -> 1.46%, 1 -> 2.21%, 2 -> 2.86% two-sided upper bounds). section: 4. Experiments - 4.8 O4 and O5: bias arm, memorization and the open-weight comparison
focus: research paper or technical report introducing the 'DeepSeek-V4' / 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash' open-weight language model
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Memorization probe (exploratory; 180 papers, 30 per disease, by date against the June 2026 cutoff; closed-book recall and guided completion; ROUGE-L and 5-gram overlap): Claude claimed specific recall for 4 papers (phenotypes only), 4 variant hits all labelled guesses and recurrent variants; the three runs of >=8 matching words are consent boilerplate; neither model reproduced the papers' variants or text; caveats (10 post-cutoff papers; black-box limits) (log §2.1.9). Table to Appendix H. Frequency deviation not started: comparator sheets unfilled; D-48 fixes the primary analysis (SSADH 363 -> 311 -> 196, HA20 769 -> 447 -> 438, Danon 505 -> 322) before any frequency is computed; LAD-I and Tangier have no comparator; result \HR{o4_deviation} (log §2.1.9). Claude vs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under an identical scaffold (HA20, SSADH): compact main-text table with span-not-found rate, values with no quote, gatekeeper unsupported overall and among claims with a quote (0.20% vs 2.28% HA20; 0.38% vs 2.03% SSADH), HGVS recall tiers 1+2 (overlapping CIs), cost per paper median ($1.08 vs $0.07; $1.19 vs $0.07) and wall-clock (log §2.1.10). State the cautions (Claude as judge; empty-quote handling; two diseases, one model, one provider; scaffold differences) and that the registered measure is pending: \HR{o5_openweight_audit}. Efficiency: expert minutes per accepted record \HR{o5_minutes_per_record}; the only measured rating times are the pilot (0.37 and 0.65 min per rating, one rater) (log §2.1.5). Exploratory GPSEA maps in one sentence: Danon reproduces the published sex difference (a reproduction check, not replication); no other disease shows a BH-significant term (log §2.1.11; table in Appendix H).
